title: Size the KV cache before it sizes you
brief: A model must serve many long conversations on a fixed GPU. The architecture, KV precision, context length and concurrency are all open. Find which dial caps concurrency, and which of your options can still move.

blocks.title: KV cache size
blocks.expr: kv_bytes = 2 x n_layers x n_kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_element x tokens x batch

vars.v: one key vector and one value vector per token
KV heads, not query heads. This is where GQA and MQA save memory
2 for fp16 or bf16, 1 for fp8, 0.5 for 4-bit
context length of each sequence times concurrent sequences

blocks.example: A Llama 3 8B shape (32 layers, 8 KV heads, head dim 128, bf16) stores 2 x 32 x 8 x 128 x 2 = **131,072 bytes, 128 KiB per token**, so 1 GiB at 8,192 tokens. A Llama 3 70B shape (80 layers, 8 KV heads, head dim 128) stores **320 KiB per token**, 2.5 GiB at 8,192 tokens. These sizes are arithmetic from the published configs [[r27]]. Every decode step reads this cache, so at long context KV bytes cap concurrency before the weights do.

blocks.intro: Start with the 7B-class MHA preset, then switch to the GQA preset and compare KV per sequence. Lower KV precision, then stretch the context. Watch the three paging rows: contiguous reservation, paged blocks, and paged blocks with a shared prefix. The shapes are illustrative, not vendor models.

blocks.title: Attention variants decide KV size at model selection
blocks.intro: You choose these when you pick a model, not later with a serving flag.

options.name: MHA
options.summary: One KV head per query head. The largest cache.
cons: KV memory and bandwidth scale with every head
Concurrency collapses first at long context
options.bestWhen: Small models or short contexts where KV is not the limit.

options.name: MQA
options.summary: All query heads share a single KV head.
pros: Smallest KV and least memory traffic
cons: Minor quality loss reported in the GQA paper [[r10]]
options.bestWhen: Decode speed and memory dominate and a small quality cost is acceptable.
options.avoidWhen: Quality-critical tasks where the loss shows up in your evals.

options.name: GQA
options.summary: A group of query heads shares each KV head, with more than one but fewer KV heads than query heads.
pros: Quality near MHA at speed near MQA after uptraining with about 5% of pre-training compute [[r10]]
cons: Still scales linearly with context and batch
options.bestWhen: General serving of dense models. It is the usual default.
options.avoidWhen: You need the largest possible cut and can adopt a latent design.

options.name: MLA
options.summary: Compress keys and values into a latent vector and cache that instead.
pros: DeepSeek-V2 reports a 93.3% smaller KV cache and 5.76x peak generation throughput versus DeepSeek 67B [[r11]]
cons: Chosen when the model is trained, not a serving flag
Needs engine support for the attention variant
options.bestWhen: You can select the model and KV memory is the binding limit.
options.avoidWhen: You must stay on an existing checkpoint with a different design.

blocks.title: Two requests sharing a prefix in paged memory
blocks.alt: Two block tables, one for request A and one for request B, both point to the same physical block holding the shared prefix. Each also points to its own private block. All blocks live in one GPU memory pool.
blocks.src:
flowchart LR
  A[Request A block table] --> S1[Block 1 shared prefix]
  B[Request B block table] --> S1
  A --> A2[Block 2 only A]
  B --> B2[Block 2 only B]
  S1 --> M[GPU block pool]
  A2 --> M
  B2 --> M
blocks.caption: Fixed-size blocks mean only the last block of a sequence can be partly empty, and identical prefix blocks are stored once [[r6]].
KV memory levers, where you set them and what limits them
head: Lever
Effect
Set at
Evidence and limits
rows: Fewer or compressed KV entries per token
KIVI at 2 bits: tuning-free, 2.6x less peak memory, up to 4x batch, 2.35x to 3.47x throughput, near-equal quality. Validate on your own long-context evals [[r20]]
PagedAttention reported 2x to 4x throughput at equal latency versus 2023 systems [[r6]]
Shared blocks stored once, prefill skipped

vLLM caches only full blocks, hashed over tokens, parent hash and extras such as LoRA id and `cache_salt`. SGLang keeps a radix tree and reported up to 6.4x throughput on structured programs [[r7]] [[r8]]
Linear: half the tokens, half the KV

items.symptom: Out of memory on long conversations although the weights loaded fine
items.cause: KV grows with context times concurrent sequences, and capacity was sized from short prompts
items.fix: Compute the KV budget as GPU memory minus reserve minus weights, then cap concurrency or context, or pick GQA or MLA, or quantize

items.symptom: Capacity plan is off by 4x to 8x for a GQA model
items.cause: The estimate used query heads instead of KV heads
items.fix: Read `num_key_value_heads` from the model config, not `num_attention_heads`

items.symptom: Throughput improved after KV quantization but long-document answers got worse
items.cause: Low-bit KV adds error that accumulates over long contexts
items.fix: Gate the change on long-context evals, keep 8-bit as the fallback, and watch quality by context length

items.symptom: One tenant can infer another's prompts by timing responses on a shared prefix cache
items.cause: Prefix blocks are shared across tenants without isolation
items.fix: Set a per-request `cache_salt` in vLLM. Treat the faster `xxhash` option with care because the doc warns about collisions and cross-tenant leakage [[r7]]

quiz.q: A model has 40 layers, 8 KV heads and head dimension 128, with fp16 KV. How many GiB of KV cache do 16 concurrent sequences of 8,192 tokens need?
quiz.hint: bytes per token = 2 x layers x kv_heads x head_dim x bytes
quiz.explain: Per token: 2 x 40 x 8 x 128 x 2 = 163,840 bytes (160 KiB). Per sequence: 160 KiB x 8,192 = 1.25 GiB. For 16 sequences: 1.25 x 16 = 20 GiB. Using 32 query heads instead of 8 KV heads would give 80 GiB, a common mistake.

quiz.q: What is wrong with this capacity estimate for a Llama-style GQA model with 80 layers, 64 query heads, 8 KV heads and head dimension 128?
options: Nothing is wrong, because the formula uses the head count the model reports
dtype_bytes should be 4, because the KV cache is stored in fp32
It multiplies by batch, but KV is shared across the whole batch
It passes query heads, so it overestimates a GQA model by 64 / 8 = 8x
quiz.explain: KV size depends on KV heads. With 8 KV heads the answer is 20 GiB, but the code prints 160 GiB. The KV cache is usually fp16 or bf16, not fp32, and each sequence has its own KV so batch multiplies the total.

quiz.q: Select the changes that reduce the KV bytes stored per token of a single sequence.
options: Use a model with 8 KV heads instead of 32
Store KV in fp8 instead of fp16
Switch the engine to PagedAttention blocks
Cache a shared system prompt with prefix caching
quiz.explain: Fewer KV heads and fewer bytes per element both shrink each token's entry. PagedAttention removes waste from over-reservation but each token still needs the same bytes. Prefix caching stores shared blocks once across sequences, which saves memory overall, but does not change the size of a token's entry.

takeaways: KV bytes per token = 2 x layers x KV heads x head dim x bytes. Use KV heads, not query heads
At long context the KV cache, not the weights, caps concurrency
GQA and MLA are model choices. Quantization, paging and prefix sharing are serving choices
KV quantization needs an eval gate because errors grow with context length
Shared prefix caches need per-tenant isolation or they leak through timing
